Choose Which Shares You Sell – Your Broker’s Default Often Means the Biggest Gain

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (457 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every purchase of a stock or fund is its own tax lot, with its own cost and date.
  • In a recent development, fidelity, Schwab, and Vanguard all use first in, first out for stocks unless you choose otherwise.
  • Say you bought a stock three times, each more than a year ago: 100 shares at $20, then 100 at $45, then 100 at $70.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every purchase of a stock or fund is its own tax lot, with its own cost and date. When you sell part of a holding, pick the high-cost lots you’ve held over a year. Brokers usually sell your oldest shares first, and those often cost the least, so they carry the biggest taxable gain.

In a recent development, fidelity, Schwab, and Vanguard all use first in, first out for stocks unless you choose otherwise. The IRS uses the same order when you can’t identify which shares you sold.

Say you bought a stock three times, each more than a year ago: 100 shares at $20, then 100 at $45, then 100 at $70. You now sell 100 at $90. First in, first out sells the $20 shares for a $7,000 gain. Choosing the $70 lot instead leaves a $2,000 gain, $5,000 less, at the same tax rate.

To choose lots for one sale, open the holding’s lot details in your account, which show each purchase’s date and cost. Then pick the lots you want on the sell order. This is called specific identification, and it overrides your default for that sale.

Industry observers note that or change the account’s default method, which brokers keep in its settings under cost basis, their term for what you paid. A highest-cost method sells your most expensive shares first but ignores how long you’ve held them. If those shares were bought within the past year, their gain is short-term and taxed at your regular income tax rate, not the lower rate on shares held more than a year. A tax-optimized method, which Schwab calls Tax Lot Optimizer and Vanguard calls MinTax, sells lots at a loss first, then long-term gains before short-term ones.

Mutual funds often default to average cost instead, which gives every share one blended price, so there’s no high-cost lot to pick. Switch a fund to another method before your first sale from it. A sale under average cost locks the shares you still hold at the averaged price, and a upcoming method covers only shares you buy later.

Set a highest-cost or tax-optimized default on each taxable brokerage account before your next sale, since any sale you don’t pick lots for uses it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, FDIC insurance covers at least $250,000 of your deposits at every insured bank.
  • Sources indicate that at the end of 2022, more than 99% of U.S.
  • It has been revealed that regulators call too-major-to-fail banks systemically key, because their collapse could drag down the economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, FDIC insurance covers at least $250,000 of your deposits at every insured bank. Up to that amount, your money is just as safe at a small bank as at a too-big-to-fail giant. Choose your bank on fees, rates, and service, and keep a larger balance fully insured rather than betting on a rescue.

Sources indicate that at the end of 2022, more than 99% of U.S. deposit accounts were under the insurance limit, the FDIC found. Only a balance above the limit could gain anything from a bank’s size, and even that gain is smaller than the too-big-to-fail label suggests.

It has been revealed that regulators call too-major-to-fail banks systemically key, because their collapse could drag down the economy. Each November the Financial Stability Board, an international body that monitors the global financial system, lists the world’s systemically important banks. Its current list includes eight from the U.S., among them JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Wells Fargo. Those banks must hold extra capital and go through the Federal Reserve’s annual stress test, a check of how their capital would hold up in a hypothetical recession. Since a 2018 law, the Fed’s stricter standards apply automatically only to banks with $250 billion or more in assets, up from $50 billion.

Those rules make a giant less likely to fail, but no law guarantees a rescue if one does. Under the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act, a failing giant the government takes over must be wound down, and taxpayer money can’t be used to keep it alive. In 2023, regulators did cover every deposit at Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, two banks not on the list. That took an exception for failures that threaten the financial system, which the Treasury secretary approved, according to their joint statement. Depositors under the limit, at any bank, needed no rescue at all.

So choose your bank on what you’ll notice: its monthly fees, the rate it pays on savings, and the help you get when something goes wrong. Banking at one of the biggest U.S. banks makes sense for branches and ATMs nearly everywhere, not for safety. Confirm any bank you consider is FDIC-insured on the FDIC’s BankFind Suite.

If you or your business keeps more than $250,000 at one bank, move the part the FDIC doesn’t insure to a second insured bank instead of counting on another exception.

Compare the best high-yield savings accounts to pick a bank by its rate and fees, not its size.

Then cut the cost of gear and fees.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you work or attend school or job training, apply to your state’s child care assistance program even if you think you earn too much, and do it early, since many states keep waiting lists.
  • According to recent reports, every state runs a child care assistance program with money from the federal Child Care and Development Fund, and each sets its own income limit, with some limits well into the middle class.
  • Federal rules cover children under 13 whose parents work or attend school or job training (under 19 for some children with disabilities or under court supervision).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you work or attend school or job training, apply to your state’s child care assistance program even if you think you earn too much, and do it early, since many states keep waiting lists. For a child under 5, apply to free Head Start or Early Head Start as well.

According to recent reports, every state runs a child care assistance program with money from the federal Child Care and Development Fund, and each sets its own income limit, with some limits well into the middle class. Vermont helps families earning up to nearly six times the federal poverty line, and New Mexico has no income limit at all.

Federal rules cover children under 13 whose parents work or attend school or job training (under 19 for some children with disabilities or under court supervision). You choose a provider that takes the subsidy, the program pays the provider, and you pay a copay, your share of the bill, which your state sets by income and family size, sometimes at zero.

It has been revealed that picture a single parent approved for her state’s program, which pays her day care everything above her copay (figures illustrative). Earning $40,000, she pays $200 a month toward a $1,100 bill, so the program saves her $10,800 a year. Her approval lasts at least 12 months, and a raise in that time can end it only by lifting her income past 85% of her state’s median income.

According to recent reports, head Start and Early Head Start are free. Head Start serves mostly 3- and 4-year-olds, and Early Head Start serves infants, toddlers, and pregnant women. Families qualify with income below the federal poverty line or with cash welfare (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or SNAP food benefits, and children in foster care or experiencing homelessness qualify at any income. Programs can fill up to 10% of spots with families above the line, and some can fill more with families under 130% of it. For a 3- or 4-year-old, check whether your state offers free public pre-K too.

The National Women’s Law Center counted over 400,000 children on child care assistance waiting lists by fall 2025, so apply now.

To apply, pick your state on Childcare.gov and open its financial assistance page, which links to your state’s program. For Head Start, enter your ZIP code in the Head Start Center Locator.

#126234. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2040 w)

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • It has been revealed that “Congratulations!
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun new way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

It has been revealed that “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Industry observers note that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

According to recent reports, so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

One of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

But occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

Sources indicate that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

Sources indicate that then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

Recent findings suggest that but eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

According to recent reports, I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

Industry observers note that then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

According to recent reports, it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Industry observers note that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning fresh things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

Industry observers note that one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

According to recent reports, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

Sources indicate that and of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

As with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

According to recent reports, we will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

*(Vine Gold is not all that useful as it turns out as 99.9% of the available items seem to be the same trinkets you see in the Silver tier).

College students have a lot on their plate already, including the need to study to get good grades, participating in any number of on-campus activities and potentially working part-time to have some spending money.

That said, college students should also focus on their financial future, including steps they can take to build credit before they enter the workforce.

After all, having a credit history and a good credit score can mean being able to rent an apartment, finance a car or take out a loan, whereas having no credit at all can mean sitting on the sidelines until the situation changes.

Fortunately, there are all kinds of ways for young adults to build credit while they’re still in school. Some strategies require a little work on their part, but many are hands-off tasks that you only have to do once.

Make sure your student knows the basic cornerstones of credit building, including the factors that are used to determine credit scores. While factors like latest credit, length of credit history and credit mix will play a role in their credit later on, the two most important problems for credit newcomers to focus on include payment history and credit utilization.

Payment history makes up 35% of FICO scores and credit utilization ratio makes up 30% of scores.

It has been revealed that generally speaking, college students and everyone else can score well in these categories by making all bill payments on time and keeping debt levels low. How low?

Most experts recommend keeping credit utilization below 30% at a maximum and below 10% for the best possible results. This means trying to owe less than $300 for every $1,000 in available credit limits at a maximum, but preferably less than $100 for every $1,000 in credit limits.

In a recent development, one step you can personally take to help a child build credit is adding them to your credit card account as an authorized user. This means they will get a credit card in their name and access to your spending limit, but you are legally responsible for any charges they make. Obviously, this move works best when you have excellent credit and a strong history of on-time payments and you plan to continue using credit responsibly .

While this step can be risky if you’re worried your college student will use their card to overspend, you don’t actually have to give them their physical authorized user credit card.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, they can get credit for your on-time payments whether they have access to a card or not. If you do decide to give them their credit card, you can do so with the agreement they can only use it for emergency expenses.

Your child can build credit faster if they apply for a credit card and get approved for one on their own, yet this can be difficult for students who have no credit history. That mentioned, secured credit cards require a refundable cash deposit as collateral are very easy to get approved for.

Sources indicate that some secured credit cards like the Ambition Card by College Ave even offer cash back1 on every purchase and don’t charge interest2. If your child opts to start building credit with a secured credit card, make sure they understand the best ways to build credit rapidly — keeping credit utilization low and paying bills early or on time each month.

While secured credit cards are a good option for students with little to no credit get started on their journey to good credit, there are also credit cards specifically designed for college students. Student credit cards are unsecured cards, meaning they don’t require an upfront cash deposit as collateral, but charge interest on any purchases not paid in full each month.

Many student credit cards offer rewards for spending with no annual fee required as well, although these cards do tend to come with a high APR. The key to getting the most out of a student credit card is having your dependent use it only for purchases they can afford and paying off the balance in its entirety each billing cycle. After all, sky high interest rates don’t really matter when you never carry a balance from one month to the next.

“One of the safest ways for college student to build their credit by learning valuable money skills.”.

While secured cards and student credit cards help young adults build credit with each bill payment they make, other payments they’re making can also help.

In fact, using an app like Experian Boost can help them get credit for utility bills they’re paying, subscriptions they pay for and even rent payments they’re making. This app is also free to use, and you only have to set up most bill payments in the app once to have them reported to the credit bureaus.

There are also rent-specific apps and tools students can use to get credit for rent payments, although they come with fees. Examples include websites like Rental Kharma and RentReporters.

The Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) also notes that students can start building credit with their student loans during school, even if they’re not officially required to make payments until six months after graduation with federal student loans.

Their advice is to make interest-only payments on federal student loans along with payments on any private student loans they have during college in order to start having those payments reported to the credit bureaus as soon as possible.

“Making interest-only payments as a student will not only positively affect your credit history but will also keep the interest from capitalizing and adding to your student loan balance,” the agency writes.

Sources indicate that of course, interest capitalization on loans would only be an issue with private student loans and  Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans since the U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on Direct Subsidized Loans while you’re in school at least half-time, for six months after you graduate and during periods of deferment.

College students don’t have to wait until they’re done with school to start building credit for the future, and it makes sense to start building positive credit habits early on regardless. Tools like a credit card can help students on their way, whether they opt for a secured credit card or a student card. Other steps like using credit-building apps can also help, and with little effort on the student’s part or on yours.

Either way, the best time to start building credit was a few years ago, and the second best time is now. You can give your student a leg up on the future by helping them build credit so it’s there when they need it.

Recent findings suggest that A customer can’t pay a bill they haven’t seen, and the days they have to pay don’t start until your invoice goes out. Send each invoice the day you finish the job, with an exact due date and a link to pay online by card or bank transfer, and call the customer the day it’s late.

Billing in one batch at the end of the month feels efficient. It also leaves a job finished on the 3rd unbilled until the 31st, four weeks in which your customer couldn’t pay you even if they wanted to.

That gap between finishing the work and sending the bill is the one delay in getting paid that you control completely. A pay-now link, which lets the customer pay from the invoice email, shortens the rest of the wait.

Picture a cleaning organization that mails its invoices at month’s end and gets paid by check, an average of 38 days after each job. Say it switches to emailing each invoice, with a pay-now link, the day the job is done. The typical bill no longer waits two weeks for the month to end or days in the mail, and customers pay without writing a check, so the average wait drops to 12 days.

Send each invoice the same day you finish, from your phone if you’re still on site. Give it an invoice number, an itemized list of the work, a due date, and payment instructions, so the customer has nothing to ask before paying. Write the due date as a date, “due March 14,” rather than “net 30,” which leaves the customer to count 30 days from the invoice date.

Add a pay-now link that accepts cards and bank transfers through ACH, the network that moves money directly between bank accounts. Cards cost you a processing fee on every payment, so ask customers with massive invoices to pay by bank transfer, which costs far less.

It has been revealed that then follow up on a schedule. Email a short reminder three days before the due date, while the customer can still pay on time. Call the day after it’s due, not a week later, so they know you track every invoice. Most invoicing apps can send the reminders automatically, so the call is the one step you have to remember.

Put that call on your calendar as you send each invoice, for the day after it’s due.

In a recent development, before you pay for preschool, check whether your state or city offers free public pre-K, and apply as soon as applications open, often months ahead. If you still need a paid program, compare co-op and part-day preschools, then pay with pretax money from a dependent care flexible spending account or claim the child and dependent care credit.

Industry observers note that florida, Georgia, and Oklahoma offer free pre-K to every 4-year-old, whatever the family earns, and so does Latest York City. Washington, D.C., offers it from age 3.

A free seat can replace a full year of tuition. Say a preschool with the same hours as a free program charges $900 a month for a nine-month school year. Taking the free seat instead saves you $8,100. Some states, though, limit free seats to children who qualify. Texas, for one, opens them to 4-year-olds who are learning English, come from lower-income families, or have a parent on active military duty, among others.

Sources indicate that check each program’s hours too. Georgia’s program runs 6.5 hours a day for 180 days, while Florida’s school-year program totals 540 hours, less than half of Georgia’s. A shorter program can still leave you paying for care for the rest of the workday.

Industry observers note that apply early. In Georgia, school systems usually take applications from January to mid-March for the next school year, and some programs fill seats by lottery. Families with lower incomes should also look into Head Start, a free federal program for young children, and their state’s child care assistance.

Sources indicate that if you’ll still pay for preschool, look for a parent cooperative, where parents take turns helping in the classroom in exchange for lower tuition. Parent Cooperative Preschools International lists member schools by state. Price a part-day or three-day schedule too, and add preschools at community centers and places of worship to your list.

For working parents, the IRS counts preschool as child care. That lets you pay for it with pretax money from a dependent care flexible spending account or claim the child and dependent care credit, though the same dollars can’t count for both.

The fall before your child would start pre-K, ask your school district whether your child qualifies, when applications open, and how many hours a day the program runs.

Recent findings suggest that before a custom order or massive project starts, take a deposit of 25% to 50% of the price, enough to buy the materials and cover the first stage of work. Put the amount and what’s refundable in the quote, and collect it before you order anything. On home improvement jobs, check whether your state limits deposits first.

It has been revealed that on a custom job, you buy the lumber, fabric, or food and put in the first hours of work before the customer pays you anything. If they back out, you’re left with materials bought for their order and the bill that came with them.

In a recent development, A deposit turns that around. Collected before you buy anything, it pays for the materials, so you work with the customer’s money instead of your own. It also commits the customer, who now has money on the line too.

Say a furniture maker quotes $4,000 for a walnut dining table whose lumber costs $1,800. He used to order the wood on a handshake. Now he asks for half, $2,000, before he orders it, so a canceled order no longer leaves him holding $1,800 of walnut he paid for himself.

According to recent reports, ask for 25% to 50% of the price, enough to cover the materials and the first stage of work. Check whether your state caps it before you quote. On home improvement work, California caps a deposit at $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less. The exception is a contractor whose bond on file with the Contractors State License Board covers all the work it has under way. Massachusetts caps a home improvement deposit at a third of the price, or the cost of special-order materials if that’s more.

On a project that runs for months, the deposit is only the first payment, and the rest comes due in stages as the work gets done.

It has been revealed that write the deposit into the quote or contract, with its due date and how much you keep if the customer cancels after you’ve ordered materials. Under the Federal Trade Commission’s Cooling-Off Rule, a customer who signs at home for a personal or household purchase can cancel for a full refund until midnight of the third business day.

Send the deposit as an invoice the customer can pay online the day they sign, and order materials only after it’s paid and any cancellation period has passed.

#126226. Industry News: Broke a CD Early? Deduct the Penalty Even If You Don’t Itemize

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (475 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Broke a CD Early? Deduct the Penalty Even If You Don’t Itemize

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (475 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the penalty for cashing in a CD early is deductible whether or not you itemize, unless the CD was in an IRA.
  • The bank reports your interest in Box 1 without taking out the penalty, so leaving Box 2 off your return means paying tax on interest the bank took back.
  • The IRS has you deduct the penalty on Schedule 1 as an adjustment to income, a deduction taken before you choose between the standard deduction and itemizing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the penalty for cashing in a CD early is deductible whether or not you itemize, unless the CD was in an IRA. Find it in Box 2 of your Form 1099-INT, apart from the interest in Box 1, and claim all of it on Schedule 1, even if it’s more than the interest.

The bank reports your interest in Box 1 without taking out the penalty, so leaving Box 2 off your return means paying tax on interest the bank took back.

The IRS has you deduct the penalty on Schedule 1 as an adjustment to income, a deduction taken before you choose between the standard deduction and itemizing. If the penalty was more than the interest earned, the part the bank took from your principal is deductible too. The IRS’s instructions for Form 1099-INT have banks include it in Box 2. A CD held in an IRA doesn’t qualify, because IRA interest isn’t taxed as it’s earned and no 1099-INT comes for it.

When you enter the 1099-INT in tax software, fill in Box 2 as well as Box 1, and the software moves the penalty to Schedule 1. On a paper return, it goes on Schedule 1’s line for the penalty on early withdrawal of savings. For some CDs longer than a year, the bank sends Form 1099-OID instead, with the penalty in Box 3.

Industry observers note that deducting the penalty also simplifies the math on breaking a CD for a better rate. It cuts the penalty’s cost by your tax rate, the same rate the extra interest is taxed at, so you can compare the two before tax. Divide the penalty by the extra interest a new CD would pay in a year to see how many years the switch takes to pay off. Say you’d pay a $300 penalty to move $20,000 from a CD with two years left into one paying a full percentage point more for those two years. The extra $200 a year earns back the $300 penalty in 18 months. By the old CD’s maturity date, it has added $400, $100 more than the $300 penalty.

Break a CD only when more time is left on it than the switch takes to pay off, and lock the upcoming rate in until the old CD would have matured.

I recently completed three of the top Christian financial education programs for churches: SeedTime’s True Financial Freedom, Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University, and Crown Financial’s MoneyLife.

Sources indicate that these popular programs all claim to help you get control of your finances from a biblical perspective. However, they go about it in different ways with varying teaching styles and philosophies.

In this post, I’ll provide an in-depth look at each program – breaking down the unique features, strengths, weaknesses, and what’s actually included when you buy in.

My goal is to give you the real deal on these courses so you can determine which one (if any) is the best fit for transforming your financial life in a way that aligns with your faith. Whether you’re deep in debt, building wealth, or simply trying to honor God with your money, this comparison will help guide your journey.

Let’s dive into the nitty-gritty details of each program:.

When it comes to pricing, Financial Peace University from Dave Ramsey sits in the middle. For an individual membership, it’s $69.99. They also offer bulk pricing for churches starting at around $800 for 10 memberships.

On the higher end, Seedtime’s True Financial Freedom charges $149 for an individual/couple license with regular deals making it available as low as $74. But they have some solid deals for Churches – you can get a bulk student license for as low as $48 per person if you buy multiple licenses. Or there’s an annual church subscription starting as low as $750 per year based on average attendance.

The most affordable option is Crown Financial’s MoneyLife course at just $29.95 for an individual purchase. I couldn’t find any publicly listed bulk pricing for churches, but being a non-profit, I’d expect them to be the cheapest route for congregations.

But as you’ll see, there are plenty more differences beyond just the price tags when comparing what’s actually included in each program.

True Financial Freedom, created by Bob Lotich and his wife Linda from SeedTime, is a financial literacy video course designed for churches that strikes a beautiful balance between biblical wisdom and practical money management strategies. The program’s goal is to equip Christians with the tools and mindset they need to experience true financial freedom while making an eternal impact for God’s Kingdom.

Industry observers note that one of the standout features of True Financial Freedom is the engaging and relatable teaching style of Bob and Linda. They share their own financial struggles and triumphs with humor, transparency, and grace, making participants feel like they’re learning from wise, caring friends rather than aloof experts. This approach creates a safe, non-judgmental environment where participants can openly discuss their financial challenges and celebrate their progress.

The program offers several unique benefits, such as the “Never 100” rule (their ‘done-is-better-than-perfect’ approach to adjust spending) and the “Straight A” strategy for automating finances. These concepts are not only memorable but also highly actionable in helping participants take control of their money and build lasting wealth.

Another strength of True Financial Freedom is its emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy. Through interactive workshops, participants are guided in developing a custom blueprint that fits their unique situation, goals, and values. This approach recognizes that there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to personal finance and empowers participants to take ownership of their financial journey.

In a recent development, true Financial Freedom is perfect for Christians who want to learn how to thrive financially while staying grounded in the Bible. The program teaches participants how to avoid the extremes of being “so heavenly-minded they’re no earthly good” or becoming so focused on building worldly wealth that they lose sight of what truly matters.

With its grace-filled approach and practical tools, True Financial Freedom helps Christians find the balance needed to change their financial life and make a lasting difference in the world in the process.

Industry observers note that financial Peace University, created by Dave Ramsey and his team at Ramsey Solutions, is a highly popular financial education program that has helped countless individuals and families get out of debt and build wealth. The program’s primary goal is to guide participants through a proven, step-by-step approach to taking control of their money and achieving financial peace.

In a recent development, dave Ramsey, the face of Financial Peace University, is known for his high-energy, tough love teaching style. He delivers hard-hitting truths about money with a sense of urgency and conviction that inspires participants to take action. However, some may find his approach a bit intense or even abrasive at times, likening it to going through bootcamp. While this style resonates with some, it may not be everyone’s preferred learning environment.

The cornerstone of Financial Peace University is the “Baby Steps” system, a clear, prescriptive plan for getting out of debt and building wealth. The program heavily emphasizes the debt snowball method, which involves paying off debts from smallest to largest, regardless of interest rates. This approach has proven highly effective in keeping participants motivated and helping them experience quick wins on their debt-free journey.

Industry observers note that while Financial Peace University does incorporate some biblical principles, its overall approach is more secular in nature. The program focuses primarily on the practical nuts and bolts of money management, with less emphasis on exploring the deeper spiritual implications of financial stewardship.

Financial Peace University is best suited for individuals and families who are drowning in debt and need a clear, actionable strategy to get back on track. The program’s structured approach and intense motivation can be a lifeline for those feeling overwhelmed by their financial situation. However, those seeking a more personalized, grace-filled approach that deeply integrates biblical wisdom may find other programs more appealing.

MoneyLife, offered by Crown Financial, is a financial education program that takes a deeply biblical approach to money management. The program’s primary goal is to guide Christians in understanding and applying God’s financial principles to their lives, emphasizing the importance of seeing God as the ultimate provider and owner of all resources.

One of MoneyLife’s distinguishing features is its strong focus on biblical teachings and spiritual practices related to money. The program dives deep into exploring how our financial decisions can reflect our faith and values, encouraging participants to align their money management with biblical principles. This emphasis on the spiritual aspects of finance sets MoneyLife apart from other programs that may focus more heavily on practical strategies.

Industry observers note that the teaching style in MoneyLife tends to be more academic and classroom-like compared to other programs. Participants can expect a significant amount of reading materials and written assessments throughout the course. While this approach may appeal to those who prefer a studious learning environment, it may not be as engaging for individuals who thrive on interactive, video-based content.

MoneyLife offers some unique elements, such as personality assessments that help participants understand how their natural tendencies impact their financial decisions. The program also includes exercises like the transfer of ownership, which guides participants in acknowledging God’s ultimate ownership of their resources. These introspective activities can be powerful tools for reshaping participants’ mindsets and habits around money.

However, one potential drawback of MoneyLife is that its emphasis on biblical principles and spiritual practices may come at the expense of providing highly actionable, practical financial strategies.

According to recent reports, moneyLife is ideal for Christians who are seeking a deeply biblical understanding of money management and are willing to engage in a more studious, reflective learning process. The program is well-suited for those who want to explore the spiritual foundations of financial stewardship and align their money habits with their faith. However, those primarily looking for a simple and easy financial strategy or a more interactive learning experience may find other programs that better fit their needs.

Having gone through all 3 programs, here is my personal experience and recommendations:.

In a recent development, I can honestly say that True Financial Freedom was a life-changing experience. Bob and Linda’s warm, relatable teaching style made me feel like I was learning from trusted friends who truly cared about my success. The program’s emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy was a game-changer for me, as it helped me develop a plan that fit my unique situation and goals.

Industry observers note that personally, True Financial Freedom struck that balance better than any of the other programs on the list and gave me the strategy to move forward. My savings, giving, and earning have all increased in significant ways since taking the program.

For those who are drowning in debt and need a clear, structured blueprint to get out, I highly recommend Financial Peace University. Dave Ramsey’s no-nonsense approach and the step-by-step “Baby Steps” system can provide the motivation and direction needed to tackle debt head-on. The debt snowball method, in particular, has helped countless people experience quick wins and build momentum on their debt-free journey. Just be prepared for a more intense, boot camp-style learning environment.

If you’re seeking a program that deeply explores the biblical principles behind money management, Crown’s MoneyLife might be the right fit for you. The program’s emphasis on spiritual practices and aligning your finances with your faith can be incredibly powerful for those who want to grow in their understanding of God’s perspective on wealth. However, be prepared for a more academic, reading-intensive learning experience and less focus on highly practical, actionable strategies.

Ultimately, the best program for you will depend on your unique financial situation, learning style, and personal goals. If you’re looking for a grace-filled, practical approach that helps you thrive in God’s Kingdom while making an eternal impact, I highly recommend True Financial Freedom. If you need a structured, intensive proposal to get out of debt fast, Financial Peace University could be your best bet. And if you desire a deep dive into the biblical foundations of money management, MoneyLife is worth considering.

Regardless of which program you choose, the most key thing is to take action and invest in your financial education. By doing so, you’ll be better equipped to handle the resources God has entrusted to you and experience the joy and freedom that comes from aligning your finances with your faith.

He lives in Greensburg, PA with his wife and two children.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that don’t wait until a months-long project ends to bill it. Tie each payment to something the client can see, like an approved design or a framed house, and write those triggers into the contract. Keep the last payment small, so most of the price is paid before the job ends.

In a recent development, waiting means you pay for the whole job before the client pays for any of it. Months of wages, subcontractor bills, and materials go out first, and a client who disputes your one invoice at the end can hold back the entire price.

According to recent reports, A milestone the client can see leaves no doubt about when a payment is due. A first draft or a framed house is either finished or not, while a trigger like “half done” invites an argument over what half means.

Recent findings suggest that then set the amounts so the money you’ve collected stays ahead of what you’ve spent. That way the client’s payments, not your own cash, cover each stage as you work through it.

A web design studio building a $24,000 website could bill in four stages and collect $19,200 by the time the build is done, instead of waiting three months to send one invoice.

The contract should name what triggers each invoice, when it’s due, and what happens when a payment is late. Two clauses keep a client from stalling your payments. One states work on each stage starts only after the previous stage’s invoice is paid. The other says a milestone counts as approved if the client hasn’t responded within five business days.

Extra requests need the same paperwork. Write each one up as a change order, a signed add-on to the contract that sets its price, before you start the work. Add that price to the next stage’s invoice instead of doing the extra work for free.

Cap the final payment at 20%, and a client who drags out the last invoice can hold back no more than a fifth of the price.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With an entire river to descend, the film wastes no time getting right into it.
  • Forty years ago, there was a road up to Lake Mayuin, the volcanic pool from with Rio Cuervo flows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This full-length adventure documentary follows kayaker Dane Jackson and a small team down Chile’s remote and wild Rio Cuervo.

With an entire river to descend, the film wastes no time getting right into it. Dane Jackson debuts into the complicated business of trip logistics, trying to find a way to get the team and their equipment to the beginning of the river. Besides him, the team consists of the trip’s mastermind, Kilian Astorga, and kayakers Tom Dolle, Eirik Hansen, Adrian Mattern, and David Sodomka.

Forty years ago, there was a road up to Lake Mayuin, the volcanic pool from with Rio Cuervo flows. It’s gone now, so they turn to helicopter transport. With their gear dangling below on a rope, the chopper carries them up into the mountain, depositing kayaks and kayakers alike on the lakeshore. They set up camp and settle in to begin the first descent of the Rio Cuervo.

It has been revealed that the team scouts the head of the river, swelled with recent rainfall. Photo: Screenshot.

It has been revealed that the dense forest and sometimes steep banks add another layer of difficulty as they begin to make their way downstream. They have to initiative ahead, as there are stretches where it is impossible to bail if the rapids become too much. This means more portaging, which is painfully slow due to the thick vegetation.

When they do hit the rapids, on-board cameras capture the frenetic energy of whitewater kayaking. But the film makes no attempt to conceal the reality of a first descent. Much of their time is spent scouting ahead by drone, poring over satellite images, portaging, and standing about debating logistics.

Sunset arrives before the end of their portage. Camping in the jungle makes for an uncomfortable night. Photo: Screenshot.

Jackson and the rest of the crew soldier on, though, cracking nerdy jokes (the jungle is compared to both Dagobah and Fangorn Forest) and making the best of bad weather and rough camping. In the final few days, conditions improve, and they can spend more time on the water.

Industry observers note that the contrast between their slow, grueling push forward and the wild speed on the river brings refreshing energy to the kayaking sections. When the river finally widens as they glide into the sea, it feels like a hard-won victory.

Running a 3.5km gorge. Photo: Screenshot.

Early in the production of a certain musical, Broadway director Harold Prince attempted to ask Andrew Lloyd Weber what the deeper political allegory or social commentary was behind the composer’s feline opus. Weber famously took a long pause and replied: “Hal, this is just about cats.”.

This movie is about kayaking. Many outdoor adventure films use the genre, and the adventure story, to explore grand themes, and some do so successfully. But when they fall flat, is it more annoying than I can begin to express. For that reason, I deeply respect the clarity of purpose evinced by Dan Jackson and First Descent Rio Cuervo.

My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • Industry observers note that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

Industry observers note that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

But a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

According to recent reports, yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

According to recent reports, one of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health company that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

In a recent development, long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

In a recent development, another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

So I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s new company, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

Sources indicate that the next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

And wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

In a recent development, it’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

According to recent reports, this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

It turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

In many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

Recent findings suggest that but there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

According to recent reports, many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

Sources indicate that while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

It has been revealed that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

And while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

Industry observers note that so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

Industry observers note that I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty quickly in the past.

But on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

According to recent reports, many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

In a recent development, since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a newly introduced, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term aims again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

When you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that indicates, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the glitch, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

The modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

Since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

Recent findings suggest that more modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

Industry observers note that my hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

It has been revealed that and it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

It has been revealed that the great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The tech giant that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

Industry observers note that I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Card fraud costs you least when you catch it the same day, not weeks later on a statement. Turn on the real-time alerts in your card’s app for every purchase, online and phone orders, foreign charges, and declined transactions, then lock the card there the moment a charge looks wrong.

Set the alerts up before your next holiday order, since the stretch from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, puts more charges than usual on your cards. A stranger’s charge is easy to miss among them when the statement arrives weeks later.

Sources indicate that A real-time alert sends each charge to your phone as it happens, so you check charges one at a time instead of a month’s worth at once. That speed matters because thieves sometimes run a small charge on a card and come back for more once it goes through, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau warns. A $1.99 charge from a merchant you’ve never heard of looks like nothing on a statement, but an alert puts it on your phone the same afternoon, and you can lock the card that minute.

On a debit card, what you can lose also grows the longer you wait to report fraud, while a credit card’s fraud protection caps your loss at $50.

In your card’s app, open the alerts or notifications settings and turn on alerts for:.

Lock the card in the app while you check any charge you don’t recognize, and report one that isn’t yours in the app or at the number on the back of the card.

Then ask for a newly introduced card number, since a lock only pauses the card and the thief still has the old one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colorado couple Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle have cycled 6,124km along the newly opened Golden Gravel Trail. The Adventure Cycling Association created the route this year to celebrate its 50th anniversary.

The trail crosses eight states — Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon — and stretches from Cape Girardeau on the banks of the Mississippi River to the small town of Port Orford on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.

Most of the route, roughly 70%, is unpaved. It is the organization’s longest off-road cycling trail, 1,120km longer than the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route.

Recent findings suggest that the Golden Gravel Trail route. Photo: The Adventure Cycling Association.

Stennes and Doyle finished in Cape Girardeau after 73 days, averaging an impressive 80km and around 12 hours of pedaling per day. “About 90% of it is mental,” they told Heartland News. “You might be tired, but you just keep on moving.”.

The couple are both experienced long-distance cyclists who have previously finished Montana’s Big Sky Spectaculaire in six days and nine hours in 2022 (a self-supported 1,400km ultra-endurance race), among other bikepacking trips.

Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle during the 2022 Massive Sky Spectaculaire. Photo: Bikepacking.com.

It has been revealed that likewise, the Adventure Cycling Association suggests riders should be self-supported for the Golden Gravel Trail. Riders are advised to carry two or three days’ worth of food for the route’s most isolated sections, and up to a day’s worth of water. This is particularly vital in the more arid sections, such as eastern Oregon. In Colorado, Utah, and Idaho, the trail traverses subranges of the Rockies and crosses the route’s highest point, Cumberland Pass at 3,668 m, in Colorado.

Stennes and Doyle say their journey included thunderstorms, aggressive farm dogs, and “countless hills.”.

Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit. Evidence indicates he fell 1,700m to his death.

Waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend. He reached the top on October 25 with guide Sonam Sherpa, but for some reason the two of them stopped descending at a rather high point on the mountain.

“The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.

In a recent development, climbers above Camp 3 on Ama Dablam. Photo: Dorjee Gyalzen Sherpa.

According to the outfitter, the climbers prepared to continue down this morning. Lama asked his client to stay in place while he returned the sleeping bag to the tent where he had borrowed it. When the Sherpa returned, Waschiczek was nowhere to be found, but his crampons were still there, which suggested a freak fall. A search helicopter was called, and the remains of the climber were found this afternoon at around 4,500m.

Waschiczek is the first fatality on Ama Dablam this season.

In a recent development, together with Manaslu, Ama Dablam is the most popular fall mountain in Nepal. The latest revision from Nepal’s Department of Tourism on October 17 showed that over 300 foreign climbers had applied for a climbing permit. That day, the rope-fixing team opened the route to the top, and a massive summit wave started a couple of days later.

Virtually all foreign climbers are guided by one or two Sherpas, so the summit rates and numbers are remarkable. Local media estimate that over 200 climbers, among locals and foreigners, have topped out so far this season. Further teams should join them over the rest of October and November. However, no matter how tamed with ropes and anchors Ama Dablam gets, a fall from its steep slopes is usually lethal.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, your business can be profitable and still run short of cash when customers pay later than your bills come due.
  • Industry observers note that your bank balance can’t show you that.
  • Industry observers note that A 13-week cash forecast lines those up by putting each payment in the week the money will actually arrive or leave.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, your business can be profitable and still run short of cash when customers pay later than your bills come due. Keep a forecast of the cash you expect in and out over the next 13 weeks, patch it every week, and you’ll see a shortfall a month or two out, in time to fix it.

Industry observers note that your bank balance can’t show you that. It shows what cleared yesterday, not what customers still owe you or the bills due next month.

Industry observers note that A 13-week cash forecast lines those up by putting each payment in the week the money will actually arrive or leave. If a customer you bill today has 30 days to pay but always takes 45 days, their payment goes in week 7, not week 5.

Take a landscaping company whose December forecast demonstrates a $14,000 shortfall in February, as winter work slows but its equipment loan and insurance bill still come due. With two months’ warning, the owner puts the insurance bill on a monthly payment plan and covers the rest for six weeks with a line of credit, a borrowing limit the company draws on as needed.

Build yours in a spreadsheet with a column for each week, and start week 1 with today’s bank balance. Add each customer payment in the week you expect the money, and subtract every payroll, rent, loan, tax, and supplier payment in the week it’s due. Each week’s ending balance becomes the next week’s starting cash.

Every week, enter what actually came in and went out beside your forecast, then add a week at the end so it always looks 13 weeks ahead. When a customer keeps paying late, move their payments to later weeks, and give any bill you forgot a row of its own.

It has been revealed that any week that ends below zero is a shortfall to start closing now. Call customers with overdue invoices, delay purchases that can wait, or arrange a business line of credit while sales still look strong to a lender. A cash reserve covers any gap those moves can’t close in time.

In a recent development, fill in your first one from your last three months of bank statements and invoices, which show how long each customer takes to pay. Then add the bills that come once or twice a year, like an insurance premium or property taxes, since three months of statements may not include them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains. This newly introduced setback comes at the height of the trekking season and also affects several climbing teams, including those engaged in alpine-style expeditions in remote areas.

Industry observers note that the first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu. Worst of all, it caused an avalanche that killed 16 Base Camp staff on Himlung. The mountain remained open to commercial expeditions despite the accident, and several guided teams are right now launching their summit pushes.

Industry observers note that manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal. Photo: Shiddi Ghising.

A low-pressure front that formed in the Bay of Bengal has now developed into a deep depression and will turn into a full cyclone tomorrow. It is expected to hit Nepal on Wednesday or Thursday through the end of the week.

The Nepal National Mountain Guides Association, in association with Senior Meteorologist Krishna Bhakta Manandhar, has put out a detailed forecast. They note that clouds spreading out from this system will hit Nepal’s mountains on October 28, especially above 6,500-7,000m in the eastern part of Nepal, including the Khumbu and Kanchenjunga regions. This will spread over the next two days, causing heavy rains throughout Nepal and snow at higher altitudes.

In a recent development, authorities and local media have urged trekkers and climbers to modify their plans and avoid river areas and high passes. The main concern is for those right now in remote areas without InReach, Starlink, or satphones.

Trekkers should check with local agencies, especially those heading for the Annapurna and Manaslu regions. Several passes there were already cut or in poor condition after the previous storm and subsequent floods.

A Russian team in the Kangchenjunga region is acclimatizing to climb 7,710m Jannu. According to their latest report, they plan to touch 7,000m before attempting their main goal.

According to recent reports, fellow Russians attempting the West Ridge of Everest have retreated to Kathmandu to rest and recover, so they should not be affected. Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov, all climbing without supplemental oxygen, are enduring some lung problems. They returned to Base Camp from their second foray up the mountain last Friday, without reaching 7,500m, as they’d hoped.

After climbing in the Cholu range, Jost Kobusch of Germany and his small team moved to the Manaslu area for the second stage of his acclimatization before attempting Everest solo in winter, also without oxygen and via the West Ridge. However, the poor state of the trails after the recent floods and the approaching cyclone have thwarted his intends.

“The flood cut our planned path and, according to forecasts, the incoming cyclone will leave up to two meters of snow,” Kobusch told ExplorersWeb from Samagaon, where the team is pondering their options.
